ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a triangle LMN: L is above, N is at the lower left, M is at the lower right, point O is located inside the triangle, and O is connected respectively to L, M, and N; what is required is ∠LOM, that is, the angle formed at point O by OL and OM. The problem states that the three angle bisectors of triangle LMN intersect at O, so O is the incenter. It is known that ∠LNM = 68°. According to the incenter angle theorem, the angle formed at the incenter by the angle bisectors pointing to the two vertices L and M satisfies ∠LOM = 90° + 1/2∠LNM. Substituting gives ∠LOM = 90° + 68°/2 = 90° + 34° = 124°.

raw_record.question_text: The three angle bisectors of triangle $L M N$ meet at a point $O$ as shown. Angle $L N M$ is $68^{\circ}$. What is the size of angle $L O M$?

method.method_draft: Use the incenter angle theorem directly. First read the image as triangle LMN with point O inside and segments OL, OM, and ON drawn from O to the three vertices; the requested angle is the angle at O between OL and OM. From the text, O is where the three angle bisectors meet, so O is the incenter, and angle LNM is 68°. Apply the theorem that for an incenter I of triangle ABC, the angle between the bisectors to vertices A and B is 90° plus half the third angle C. Here ∠LOM is between the L- and M-bisectors, so it equals 90° + 68°/2 = 124°.

method.method_draft: Derive the needed angle from half-angles in triangle LOM. From the image, note that O lies inside triangle LMN and the target ∠LOM is an interior angle of smaller triangle LOM, with sides LO and MO drawn to vertices L and M. From the text, LO and MO are angle bisectors, so ∠OLM is half of the full angle at L and ∠OML is half of the full angle at M. Since ∠LNM = 68°, the other two full angles of triangle LMN sum to 180° − 68° = 112°. Therefore the two base angles of triangle LOM at L and M sum to half of 112°, which is 56°. Then use the angle sum in triangle LOM: ∠LOM = 180° − 56° = 124°.

Reasoning: Since the three angle bisectors of triangle LMN meet at O, LO bisects the angle at L and MO bisects the angle at M. Given ∠LNM = 68°, the other two angles of triangle LMN sum to 180° − 68° = 112°. Therefore, in triangle LOM, the angles at L and M are half of those two angles, so their sum is 112° ÷ 2 = 56°. Using the angle sum of triangle LOM, ∠LOM = 180° − 56° = 124°.
